why: Commit 1 is named against the code (part-styles.tsx lines 45 and 62, the three Kaizena Flow roots at their lines, the six admin files that import row components), but it moves a sheet every responsive row depends on into the layouts and touches about twelve files. A place drawing rows where no layout draws the sheet loses its breakpoint classes and is caught only if an e2e spec happens to view it at the right width. Commit 2 is optional and its keep-or-drop rule includes an observation no check makes ('a page shows unstyled rows for a moment on a slow load'), and both commits lower budgets to whatever the build measures.
harm_if_wrong: Rows on some store, platform or preview page would lose their phone/desktop classes (a header showing the desktop menu on a phone) on every page of that kind, while unit tests and the touched e2e specs pass.
make_it_cheaper: Replace commit 2's 'drop it if styles arrive late' with a concrete check (for example an e2e case that throttles the network and asserts every row has its kzr- rules before first paint), or move commit 2 out to its own step; commit 1 then remains review only for its breadth.
brief_problems: The scan test's ALLOWED list names src/components/admin/page-builder.tsx, but that file does not import any of the five row modules, so the entry is dead.
drawing.tsx and editor-views.tsx are left to 'read the file; use the owner its place uses' and 'any other that draws …', which are small per-component judgements rather than named edits.
The e2e budget edits ('lower to the figure this build measures plus the margin') turn expectations into recorded values.
